svg.title: Four Government Datasets Held, Not Published — Accountability Voids
svg.desc: Schematic analysis of four critical public data absences: chassis-level crash registry, hospital trauma linkage, operator-linked FIRs, and route-permit beneficial ownership.
svg.text: DATA ARCHITECTURE AUDIT · SCHEMATIC (NOT A MAP)
Four Datasets Held, Not Published: The Accountability Voids
Key government-held records that would prove, calibrate, or disprove systemic road transport failures

g.text: VOID-01 · BRTA VEHICLE REGISTRY
Chassis-Level Crash Log
Crashes logged by surface plate number, not persistent chassis.
Chassis numbers remain unlinked across re-registrations.
Would test: Phoenix fleet ownership continuity and banned hardware return.
VOID-02 · HEALTH & POLICE LINKAGE
Hospital Trauma Admissions
Emergency trauma and post-admission deaths are never matched
to police crash records or road injury reports.
Would test: The 5.8× undercount between FIR-only logs and 30-day mortality.
VOID-03 · POLICE FIR RECORDS
Operator-Linked Crash FIRs
Police First Information Reports record individual drivers only,
omitting corporate fleet operator identities and permit holders.
Would test: Corporate and institutional liability versus isolated driver blame.
VOID-04 · REGULATORY COMMERCE
Route Permit Beneficial Ownership
Regional Transport Committee (RTC) route permits are held
through unregistered associations, proxies, and front entities.
Would test: Political patronage and regulatory capture across bus corridors.

svg.text: Bureau finding: Each void is an administrative and regulatory reporting choice, not a technical data collection limit.
